Illustration of a spring balance (Newton meter). A tubular casing with a hook at the top for suspension and a hook at the bottom where a load is attached. Inside the casing, a coiled spring is visible or implied, connected to an indicator (pointer) that slides along a vertical scale on the outside of the casing. The scale is marked in Newtons (N) and usually grams (g) or kilograms (kg). Clean flat textbook illustration, white background.

A line graph showing a Force (y-axis) against extension (x-axis) curve for a typical metal wire. The curve starts as a straight line from the origin to a point 'P' (Proportional limit). Shortly after 'P' is point 'E' (Elastic limit), where the line begins to curve. Further along is point 'Y' (Yield point) where the curve dips slightly and flattens out, indicating plastic flow. The curve then rises to a peak 'M' (Maximum load or Ultimate tensile strength), and finally ends at a lower point 'B' (Breaking point) where the wire snaps. Clean flat textbook illustration, white background.
